<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:fast-fast_slow-slow_makes_no_difference}
    With the notation above, $T_{N, m}^*\stackrel{d}{=} T_{N, m}$. 
    
    More generally, the same distributional identity stands for arbitrary overtake rates
    between pairs of fast and pairs of slow particles.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:sorting_time}
    With the notation above, considering the independent coupling for $N=1, 2, \dots$,
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:main1}
    \frac{T_{N, m}}{N}\xrightarrow{a.s.}\frac{1}{K}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}\frac{1}{z-v_i}+\sum_{i=m}^{K-1}\frac{1}{v_i-z}\right) \quad m=1,2, \dots, K-1,
    \end{equation}
    and hence taking maximum,
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:main2}
    \frac{T_N}{N}\xrightarrow{a.s.}
    \frac{1}{K}\max_{1\leq m<K}\inf_{v_{m-1}<z<v_{m}}
    \left(
        \sum_{i=0}^{m-1}\frac{1}{z-v_i}+\sum_{i=m}^{K-1}\frac{1}{v_i-z}
    \right).
    \end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
For even $K$, let the set of speeds be $\{i/K\}_{i=1}^{K}$. Then the infimum is maximal for $m=K/2$ in which case it is attained at $z=\frac{K-1}{2}$, and we obtain
    $$\frac{T_N}{N}\to 2\sum_{i=0}^{K/2-1}\frac{1}{i+1/2}\sim_{K\to\infty} 2\log(K/2).$$
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- example-2: body_md -->
For even $K$ and $\beta>1$, let the set of speeds be $\{\pm \beta^i\}_{i=0}^{K/2-1}$. The infimum is maximal again for $m=K/2$, in which case it is attained at $z=0$, and we obtain
    $$\frac{T_N}{N}\to 2\sum_{i=0}^{K/2-1}\beta^{-i}\to_{K\to\infty}2\left(1-\frac{1}{\beta}\right).$$
<!-- end example-2 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:exponential-block}
Consider an LPP in the vertices of the positive quadrant with parameters
$\tau_{(a,b)}\sim\operatorname{Exp}(x_a+y_b)$, where $x_a+y_b>0$ for every $a,b$.  The law of $T_\sigma^*$ is
invariant under permutations of the $x$-parameters in a column block and of
the $y$-parameters in a row block.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
\cite[Theorem~3.1]{BatesEmrahMartinSeppalainenSorensen2026} tells us that in the setup of the Lemma, permuting column parameters in an interval $[a, a']$ of columns does not change the joint law of passage times $\{L_p^q:p_1, q_1\notin (a, a')\}$. However, inspecting \eqref{eq:boundary-lpp} this implies the invariance of $T_\sigma^*$ for such permutations of the parameters.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lemma:in_block_exchange_invariance}
In the suppressed model, the law of $T_\sigma^*$ is invariant under
permuting labels inside any block of fast particles or inside any block of
slow particles.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
For an arbitrary configuration $\sigma$, its fast--slow projection
determines the corresponding Young diagram, while the order of the fast
and slow labels determines the assignment of the $x$-parameters to its
columns and of the $y$-parameters to its rows. Thus permuting labels inside
a particle block amounts precisely to permuting the corresponding
$x$-parameters in a column block or the $y$-parameters in a row block.
The claim follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:exponential-block}.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lemma:deterministic_scenario_independence}
    $T_{\sigma}^{*,\Sigma}\stackrel{d}{=} T_{\sigma}^*$ for any finite $\Sigma$ and initial condition $\sigma\in S_N$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
We do induction on $|\Sigma|$, for $|\Sigma|=0$ the statement is tautological. 
    
    Consider now $|\Sigma|=s$ above. Let $\sigma(t_1)\in S_N$ be the state at time $t_1$ right before the (potential) interchange at time $t_1$, and for $\sigma'\in S_N$, denote by $(a_1\leftrightarrow b_1)\circ \sigma'$ the state obtained by interchanging $a_1, b_1$, if they are adjacent.
    \begin{align*}
    T_{\sigma}^{*,\Sigma}&=\mathbf{1}_{T_{\sigma}^{*,\Sigma}<t_1} T_{\sigma}^{*,\Sigma}+\mathbf{1}_{T_{\sigma}^{*,\Sigma}>t_1}\sum_{\sigma'\in S_N}\mathbf{1}_{\sigma(t_1)=\sigma'}\left(t_1+T_{(a_1\leftrightarrow b_1) \circ \sigma'}^{*,\Sigma-(t_1, a_1, b_1)}\right) \\
    &\stackrel{d}{=}\mathbf{1}_{T_{\sigma}^*<t_1} T_{\sigma}^*+\mathbf{1}_{T_{\sigma}^*>t_1}\sum_{\sigma'\in S_N}\mathbf{1}_{\sigma(t_1)=\sigma'}\left(t_1+T_{(a_1\leftrightarrow b_1)^ \circ \sigma'}^*\right)
    \\ 
    &\stackrel{d}{=} \mathbf{1}_{T_{\sigma}^*<t_1} T_{\sigma}^*+\mathbf{1}_{T_{\sigma}^*>t_1}\sum_{\sigma'\in S_N}\mathbf{1}_{\sigma(t_1)=\sigma'}\left(t_1+T_{ \sigma'}^*\right) \\
    &\stackrel{d}{=} T_{\sigma}^*,
    \end{align*}
    where in the first $\stackrel{d}{=}$ we used the induction hypothesis and the fact that the conditional distribution of $T_{\sigma}^*$ and $T_{\sigma}^{*,\Sigma}$ coincides on stopping before $t_1$, 
    and in the second $\stackrel{d}{=}$, we used Lemma \ref{lemma:in_block_exchange_invariance}. This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Initialize Poisson clocks of appropriate parameters for every pair of fast and every pair of slow particles. The ringing times of these give rise to a scenario in the sense of \Cref{lemma:deterministic_scenario_independence}. Applying it, we see that the conditional distribution of $T_\sigma$ with respect to any scenario is identical to the distribution of $T_{\sigma}^*$. Hence by Fubini, $T_\sigma \stackrel{d}{=} T_{\sigma}^*$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Now we return to our problem with $K$ types as $N\to \infty$. According to \Cref{thm:fast-fast_slow-slow_makes_no_difference}, for fixed $N$ the $m$-sorting 
time $T_{N, m}$ starting from reverse-speed configuration can be modeled by a last passage time from 
$(1, 1)$ to $\left((K-m)n, mn\right)$. A subtle difficulty concerning the asymptotics of its last passage time is that different $N$s 
correspond to a different environment. However by our findings we can use a single environment to model $T_{N, m}$ for every $N$:
set
\[
    x_a=v_{m+((a-1)\bmod (K-m))},
    \qquad
    y_b=-v_{m-1-((b-1)\bmod m)}.
\]
In this single environment, for every $K, n$ we have 
$L^{\left((K-m)n, mn\right)} \stackrel{d}{=} T_{N, m}$.


Invoking \cite[Theorem~3.2]{EJS2021}, we find that
$$\frac{L^{\left((K-m)n, mn\right)}}{N}\xrightarrow{a.s.} \frac{1}{K}\inf_{v_{m-1}<z<v_{m}}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{m-1} \frac{1}{z-v_i}+\sum_{i=m}^{K-1} \frac{1}{v_i-z}\right).$$
As this result is proved via summable tail bounds, we obtain \eqref{eq:main1} by the distributional identity we proved. Taking maximum for $m$ yields \eqref{eq:main2}.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
